$schema.description: The JSON Schema of this file, for editors: a path relative to the file (e.g. ../schemas/experiment.schema.json, as 'stratarec schema --out schemas' writes them) or a URL. The engine ignores it: it is not part of the file's content id.

expires_at.description: ISO date (yyyy-MM-dd) after which the experiment may not enter new manifests.

arms.description: Arm id → RFC 7396 merge patch; control arms are usually {}.

additionalProperties.description: An RFC 7396 merge patch of the pipeline and catalog: an object changes only the members it names, null deletes, an array is replaced whole. A new node or entry must be complete; 'stratarec validate' checks what the patch does to the baseline.

params.description: Parameter values; map-typed parameters are nested objects flattened to leaves.

type.description: int64, float64, bool, string or map<string,T>.

columns.description: Candidate columns nodes write, one value per candidate, read as col.<name>.

flow.description: Flow columns may be rewritten by later nodes on the same path.

default.description: Replacement for non-finite numeric writes; required for non-nullable numeric columns.

request_columns.description: Request columns nodes write, one value per request, read as req.<name> by what runs after the node that writes one: a later node's expressions and when, a log tap, the output's columns and values (not a funnel key, decided when the request starts, nor a derived feature). Written by RequestAggregate@1 (a count, sum, mean, min or max over the live candidates) or by a custom operator. Declared as candidate columns are (type, default, flow): a value no node wrote is missing, and a non-nullable one needs a node that cannot be skipped to write it before every reader. Experiments may add request columns, not change these.

flow.description: Flow columns may be rewritten by later nodes on the same path.

default.description: Replacement for non-finite numeric writes; required for non-nullable numeric columns.

order.description: Semantic position; required unless role is fallback.

op.description: Operator type and version, e.g. TopK@1.

timeout_ms.description: Milliseconds one attempt of the node may take, at least 1; it never gets more than is left of the request's deadline. Past it the attempt fails as a timeout, and on_failure decides what follows. Default: what is left.

min_remaining_ms.description: The node is skipped, as by a false when, when less than this many milliseconds are left of the request's deadline as it is about to start: for a node not worth starting late. Default: it starts whatever is left.

on_failure.description: What a failure of this node does: fail_request (default) fails the request, skip goes on without the node's writes, fallback runs the node named by fallback in its place.

fallback.description: With on_failure fallback: the node, declared with "role": "fallback", that runs when this one fails.

fallback_reserve_ms.description: With on_failure fallback: milliseconds of the request's remaining time this node leaves to its fallback. Default: the fallback's timeout_ms, or 0 when it has none.

role.description: fallback for nodes that only run as another node's fallback.

config.description: score = base × Π multipliers + Σ addends, with named, independently patchable terms.

multipliers.description: Named multipliers; experiments add, change or delete (null) single entries without conflicts.

config.description: Drops rows for which a boolean ColumnExpr predicate is false.

predicate.description: Non-nullable bool ColumnExpr; rows where it is false are dropped.

config.description: Evaluates a ColumnExpr for every live row and writes it to a column.

output_col.description: Column to write (declared under columns); may be a flow column read by expr.

expr.description: The ColumnExpr computed for every row. Its result has the output column's type, and may be missing only if the column is nullable: the row's value is then missing.

config.description: Appends the candidates a generative model names that the table does not have, from prompts rendered with Mustache templates.

model.description: Logical model name, bound per environment.

version.description: Fixed model version; or use version_param.

version_param.description: String parameter (with an enum of allowed versions) selecting the version per request.

output.description: The model's text output holding the answer: a JSON array of entity ids (integers for int64 keys, strings for string keys).

max_items.description: The most rows the node appends: the first new ids of the answer. Also the node's row limit, which sizes the request's candidate table.

rank_col.description: A column for each appended row's 1-based position in the answer: int64? or int32? (undeclared: int64?). Rows the node did not append have no value in it.

max_output_tokens.description: The most tokens the model may generate, passed with the call.

config.description: Per group of rows (by a column, or all rows): count, sum, mean, min, max, std or rank, written back to every row of the group.

group_col.description: Grouping column (int64, int32 or string), e.g. item.author_id. Omitted, all rows form one group. A row whose key is missing is in no group: its outputs are missing.

outputs.description: Output column → what it gets. An object, so an experiment adds, changes or deletes (null) one output. A column not declared under columns is declared by the node: int64 for count and rank, float64 for the others, nullable when a value can be missing.

fn.description: count (rows of the group), sum, mean, min, max, std (population standard deviation) of value_col, or rank: the row's 1-based place in its group, ordered by value_col as TopK@1 orders (missing last, ties by entity_id ascending).

value_col.description: Numeric column the function reads; count takes none. Missing values are left out (a column holds no NaN: a commit makes non-finite values the default or missing).

config.description: Reranks the leading rows by scores a model gives them as one list.

model.description: Logical model name, bound per environment.

version.description: Fixed model version; or use version_param.

version_param.description: String parameter (with an enum of allowed versions) selecting the version per request.

output.description: The model output read: float32 or float64 [1, -1], one score per row of the list, higher first.

window.description: The leading ranks sent as one list and reordered by their scores; later rows keep their order after them.

score_col.description: Optional column for each window row's score: float32? or float64?, missing outside the window. An undeclared column is float32?.

config.description: Writes a generative model's answer for each leading row into a column, from prompts rendered per row with Mustache templates.

model.description: Logical model name, bound per environment.

version.description: Fixed model version; or use version_param.

version_param.description: String parameter (with an enum of allowed versions) selecting the version per request.

output.description: The model's text output holding the answer: the row's value.

column.description: The column written: nullable, since the rows after the window and the rows whose answer is not usable have no value. string?, bool?, int32?, int64?, float32? or float64?; an undeclared column is string?.

categories.description: For a string? column: the answers it allows, compared exactly; any other answer is not usable.

window.description: The leading rows annotated, one model call each; the rows after them stay missing.

max_output_tokens.description: The most tokens the model may generate per answer, passed with each call.

config.description: Reranks the leading rows in the order a generative model lists them, from prompts rendered with Mustache templates.

model.description: Logical model name, bound per environment.

version.description: Fixed model version; or use version_param.

version_param.description: String parameter (with an enum of allowed versions) selecting the version per request.

output.description: The model's text output holding the answer: a JSON array of window ranks or entity ids (see answer).

window.description: The leading rows the prompts show and the answer may reorder; later rows keep their order after them.

answer.description: What the answer lists: rank, the 1-based window positions {{rank}} shows, or entity_id, the rows' entity ids (JSON integers for int64 keys, strings for string keys). No default: the prompt decides.

unlisted.description: Window rows the answer does not list: keep them after the listed ones, in their previous order, or drop them.

max_output_tokens.description: The most tokens the model may generate, passed with the call.

config.description: Maximal marginal relevance rerank of the leading rows using an embedding column.

embedding_col.description: A fixed-length float list column (list<float32,N> or list<float64,N>), such as an item embedding; rows without one have zero similarity to everything.

lambda.description: Relevance weight λ in [0, 1]; use lambda_param to make it tunable.

lambda_param.description: A float64 parameter for λ, declared with a min and a max within [0, 1].

window.description: Number of leading ranks to rerank; later rows keep their order. Default 50.

config.description: Scores rows with a model: named inputs from columns, named outputs to columns, batched.

model.description: Logical model name, bound per environment.

version.description: Fixed model version; or use version_param.

version_param.description: String parameter (with an enum of allowed versions) selecting the version per request.

outputs.description: Model output name → column to write, whose declared type is the output's tensor type (as an input's is).

batch_size.description: Most rows per model call: the rows are split into the fewest calls, of even size, which run concurrently.

config.description: Concurrent multi-source retrieval with deterministic merge and entity_id dedup.

quotas_param.description: Map parameter source name → quota (e.g. recall_quotas); a quota of 0 disables a source.

source_order.description: Merge order of sources: the listed ones first, then the others by name (all by name without it). Earlier sources win the primary source. An experiment adds a source by giving it a quota, and lists it here to move it ahead.

queries.description: Per source, the values its query sends, its call's only inputs: value name → a request-level expression over ctx.* and param.*, such as { "two_tower": { "user_embedding": "ctx.user.embedding" } } for a two-tower service that needs the user's features to retrieve. A source waits for the context features its own query reads and for nothing else: one without a query starts at once, one reading the user's embedding as soon as it is stored (a derived feature as soon as it is computed), while the others run; sources whose features are stored together are sent in source order. The wait is within the node's budget. A source whose query reads a feature that failed is not called, as soon as that feature failed, and counts as a failed source; a degraded one degrades the node; a missing value is sent as missing.

config.description: Reranks the leading rows by a model's pairwise preferences, aggregated into expected wins.

model.description: Logical model name, bound per environment.

version.description: Fixed model version; or use version_param.

version_param.description: String parameter (with an enum of allowed versions) selecting the version per request.

output.description: The model output read: float32 or float64 [-1], one value per pair, the probability that the pair's first (higher-ranked) row is preferred.

window.description: The leading ranks to rerank (at least 2); later rows keep their order after them.

max_pairs.description: Load-time ceiling on the pairs a request sends: window · (window − 1) / 2 above it is a config error. Every pair in the window is compared; none is dropped at run time. The default allows a window of 50.

batch_size.description: Most pairs per model call: the pairs are split into the fewest calls, of even size, which run concurrently.

score_col.description: Optional column for each window row's aggregated score (its expected wins against the other rows of the window): float32? or float64?, missing outside the window. An undeclared column is float32?.

config.description: Calls a pipeline for each row and writes what it returns into the row's columns: its rows as lists, its values as values.

pipeline.description: The pipeline every row calls. With pipelines, the one for the rows none of its entries is for; without either, such a row calls nothing and gets no values.

by.description: What says which entry of pipelines a row calls: a row-level expression of a string or an integer, such as col.kind. Without it, the row's key (col.entity_id).

pipelines.description: The pipelines by the value of by, such as { "ads": { "pipeline": "sponsored" } }: rows of different kinds call different pipelines, all at once. What the node writes (ids, columns, values) is every entry's, which may add to it and replace it by name; how a pipeline is called (inputs) is its own.

inputs.description: Inputs to pass to this pipeline, as the node's inputs are to pipeline.

ids.description: The column that gets the ids, when not the node's ids.

columns.description: Lists to fill besides the node's columns, such as an output column only this pipeline has ({ "track_ids": "track_id" }); one for the same list replaces the node's.

values.description: Values to take besides the node's values; one for the same column replaces the node's.

cache.description: Caches the results of this pipeline's calls, as the node's cache does those of pipeline.

ttl_ms.description: Required: how long a result is served, in milliseconds, e.g. 3600000. Each result's lifetime varies by ±10% with its key, so results computed together do not all expire together.

stale_if_error_ms.description: How much longer (milliseconds, default 0) an expired result may be served when the pipeline fails now; the node is then degraded.

version.description: Names what the cached results are computed by, e.g. "3". Without it the cache follows the called pipeline's configuration: a release that changes its pipeline or catalog, the data or services it is bound to, or an experiment the request is in, computes anew. With it the results are kept across such releases, until the name changes. Letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', at most 64.

inputs.description: Inputs to pass to pipeline: its input name → an expression, which may read the row (col.*), such as { "genre": "col.genre" }. Every other input the called pipeline declares gets this request's input of the same name, when it has one. An entry of pipelines has inputs of its own.

ids.description: The column (list<int64> or list<string>, as the called pipeline's keys are, declared under columns) that gets the ids of the rows the call returned, in their order.

columns.description: Lists to fill: this pipeline's list column (declared under columns) → the called pipeline's output column, such as { "game_scores": "score" }. Element i of each list is of the row whose id is element i of ids. The output column must have a value on every row: a list has no missing elements.

values.description: Values to take: this pipeline's column (declared under columns) → the called pipeline's output value (output.values), such as { "best": "score.best" }.

max_calls.description: The most rows it calls for, 1 to 1000: the first ones in rank order. Required: every row is a run of a pipeline, so the node says how many it may start. The rows after them get no values, and the node is degraded.

timeout_ms.description: The deadline of each called run, in milliseconds from when it is called; without it, what the node has left. It is the called pipeline's deadline as a request's is: a pipeline that fails when it runs out of time fails the call, and its row gets no values; one that serves what it has by then (a node of its own with on_failure: skip) answers with that.

cache.description: Caches the results of pipeline's calls, each by the inputs its row passes: while a result is cached the pipeline does not run for that row, such as { "ttl_ms": 3600000 }. The environment says where the results are kept (pipelines.<id>.cache in the bindings). An entry of pipelines has a cache of its own.

ttl_ms.description: Required: how long a result is served, in milliseconds, e.g. 3600000. Each result's lifetime varies by ±10% with its key, so results computed together do not all expire together.

stale_if_error_ms.description: How much longer (milliseconds, default 0) an expired result may be served when the pipeline fails now; the node is then degraded.

version.description: Names what the cached results are computed by, e.g. "3". Without it the cache follows the called pipeline's configuration: a release that changes its pipeline or catalog, the data or services it is bound to, or an experiment the request is in, computes anew. With it the results are kept across such releases, until the name changes. Letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', at most 64.

computed_by.description: Columns written on each row whose call returned, that say which request's run computed what the row got, such as { "request_id": "games.request_id" }. Every entry's.

request_id.description: The column (string?) that gets the id of the request whose run computed the result.

time_ms.description: The column (int64?) that gets that request's time, in Unix milliseconds.

config.description: Calls another pipeline for the request and appends the rows it returns as candidates.

pipeline.description: The pipeline to call: one the engine serves, of this pipeline's entity_key_type.

inputs.description: Inputs to pass: the called pipeline's input name → a request-level expression (ctx.*, req.*, param.*), such as { "slots": "param.ad_slots" }. Every other input the called pipeline declares gets this request's input of the same name, when it has one.

limit_param.description: Parameter holding the most rows to append: the result's first rows the request has not seen yet, so a row already there does not use one up. Required, as every row source's limit is: it bounds the rows a request may hold . A parameter without a value (a map's key set to null) appends none.

columns.description: Columns to copy: this pipeline's column (declared under columns) → the called pipeline's output column, such as { "ad.bid": "bid" }. Written on the appended rows only.

mark.description: A bool column written true on the appended rows, to tell them from the others, which have no value in it: read it as col.x ?? false. Undeclared, it is declared bool?; declared, declare it bool? (a default does not fill the rows of other row sources).

cache.description: Caches the call's result: while a result is cached the pipeline does not run, such as { "ttl_ms": 3600000 }. The environment says where the results are kept (pipelines.<id>.cache in the bindings).

ttl_ms.description: Required: how long a result is served, in milliseconds, e.g. 3600000. Each result's lifetime varies by ±10% with its key, so results computed together do not all expire together.

stale_if_error_ms.description: How much longer (milliseconds, default 0) an expired result may be served when the pipeline fails now; the node is then degraded.

version.description: Names what the cached results are computed by, e.g. "3". Without it the cache follows the called pipeline's configuration: a release that changes its pipeline or catalog, the data or services it is bound to, or an experiment the request is in, computes anew. With it the results are kept across such releases, until the name changes. Letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', at most 64.

computed_by.description: Columns written on the appended rows that say which request's run computed them, such as { "request_id": "rank.request_id" }.

request_id.description: The column (string?) that gets the id of the request whose run computed the result.

time_ms.description: The column (int64?) that gets that request's time, in Unix milliseconds.

config.description: Over the live candidates: count, sum, mean, min or max of an expression, written to request columns (req.*).

values.description: Request column (declared under request_columns) → what it gets, over the live candidates when the node runs. An object, so an experiment adds, changes or deletes (null) one value.

fn.description: count (the rows; with of, the rows where it has a value), sum, mean, min or max of of over the rows where it has a value. Missing values are left out, as SQL's aggregates leave out nulls, and with no value to aggregate every function but count is missing.

of.description: The numeric ColumnExpr aggregated per row, e.g. col.score.final; count takes it optionally. An integer one sums, and has a min and max, as an integer; a float one as a float; a mean is a float.

where.description: A predicate (a non-nullable bool, as ExpressionFilter@1's): only the rows where it holds are aggregated, e.g. col.recall.primary_source == 'popular'.

config.description: Limits rows per group within any sliding window of ranks; over-quota rows move down or drop.

group_col.description: Grouping column (int64, int32 or string), e.g. item.creator_id. Missing values are never limited.

max_per_window.description: Maximum rows of one group in any window.

config.description: Sorts rows by a score column (missing last, ties by entity_id) and keeps the first k.

k.description: Fixed number of rows to keep; use k_param to make it tunable.

key.description: Key expressions; the first non-missing value is the sampling key.

columns_from.description: Expands to the named inputs of a node whose operator maps expressions to them (the model operators, or a custom operator's), e.g. ctr_ranker.inputs: the tap logs those expressions, evaluated at its own point.

fetch_missing.description: Reserved: only false is accepted. A tap never triggers a fetch; it logs what the serving path fetched before its point.

field.description: Physical field name in the store.

default.description: Value used when the key legitimately has no value; makes the feature non-nullable.

reviewed_interactions.description: Interactions with experiments of other layers that were reviewed and may happen together: experiment id → the columns, e.g. { "exp_freshness_calibration": ["score.final"] }, a request column written as req.<name>. The two experiments' interaction warnings on those columns are not repeated, so a reviewed pair stops warning on every validate, build and load; a new column still warns. An entry no interaction of this release needs is a warning, so a review does not outlive the interaction it was for. It lives with the experiment, not the release file, because the manifest carries it.
